VAL-APP-001.evidence: POST /api/applications/bulk/delete with {"ids":["app-008"]} returned 200 with {"success":true,"message":"Deleted 1 application(s)"}. Subsequent GET /api/applications returned 7 apps; app-008 was not present in the list.

VAL-APP-002.evidence: After POST /api/applications/bulk/archive with {"ids":["app-006"]} returned 200, GET /api/applications showed app-006 with "archived":true.

VAL-APP-003.evidence: POST /api/applications/bulk/transfer with {"ids":["app-007"],"newOwner":"QA Team"} returned 200. GET /api/applications/app-007 showed "owner":"QA Team".

VAL-APP-004.evidence: After archive (app-006) and transfer (app-007) mutations, GET /api/applications returned all 8 apps (pre-delete) with app-006 archived:true and app-007 owner:"QA Team". Mutations persisted across separate GET requests within the same server session, confirming mutable in-memory store.

VAL-APP-005.evidence: POST /api/applications/bulk/archive with {"ids":["app-006"]} returned HTTP 200 (not 400). The {"ids":[...]} request body format is accepted correctly, confirming frontend-backend contract alignment.

VAL-APP-006.evidence: After bulk deleting app-008, GET /api/applications/app-008 returned HTTP 404 with statusMessage "Application not found".
